author.name: Zac Kyoti
credits: Zac Kyoti: Direct Jump's design, its ColdFire source and the MKI hardware work behind it. Sam Banks: octabam integration.
Modwerk contributors: source import with stock guards in place of stock bytes, the emulator gate, documentation and SVG thumbnail.

presentation.label: Clock-locked pattern jump on [PTN] + [YES]
presentation.summary: Hold [PTN] and press [YES] to turn Direct Jump Kyoti on: a pattern you cue takes over on the next step, where it would be had it played since PLAY or the last normal pattern change.
presentation.overview: On the stock OS a cued pattern waits for the playing one to reach its end. With Direct Jump on, it takes over on the next step instead, locked to the master clock: it starts at the step it would be on had it been playing since you pressed PLAY, or since the last normal pattern change, whatever its length, scale or per-track settings. Trig conditions carry on as if the new pattern had played all along, each track gets its new Part settings with its own first trig, and with SILENCE TRACKS on the tracks a jump silences are released before the step instead of cut. It is off at every power-on, so the stock behaviour stays the default. It is Zac Kyoti's design, distinct from octabam's other direct jump (Tim Hastie's CHAIN AFTER option).
highlights: OS 1.40C. Zac Kyoti ran this Modwerk build (its native card image) on his MKI on 17 November 2026: all 13 checks of his list passed. On 19 November 2026 he ran its USB package on the same MKI: install, jumps, a power cycle, removal and a rolled-back trial passed. Not yet run on an MKII.
Off at every power-on: until you turn it on, pattern changes are the stock ones.

The new pattern lands where it would be had it played since PLAY or the last normal pattern change, also with differing track lengths and scales (PER TRACK mode), so tracks stay in phase with the master clock: after a normal change to a 12-step pattern, a jump to another 12-step pattern lands on the step the first was on. It lands a tick before the step, so its first step is never late, and a cue in the playing pattern's last step lands on its grid point too.
Trig conditions carry on across a jump: every A:B count stands where the new pattern's would, counted from that same restart; a latched [FILL] stays on, and a PRE trig right after the jump plays.

The Part's pattern-wide settings and START SILENT change as on a stock pattern change. With LFO AUTO CHANGE on, each track's new LFO settings arrive with its first trig of the new pattern, so a sound still ringing keeps its own.
With SILENCE TRACKS on, the tracks a jump silences are released with stock's note-off just before the step, so they do not pop.
The last MIDI Program Change names the pattern that plays; no MIDI START is sent on a jump.
Includes Zac Kyoti's fix for stock's MIDI Plays-Free stall, so a Plays Free MIDI track in PER TRACK mode keeps playing and Direct Jump places it with its own scale.
The arranger and pattern chains are left alone: while either runs, pattern changes are stock.
usage: Hold [PTN] and press [YES]: DIRECT JUMP ON appears. Release [PTN]; the pattern chooser stays shut.
Press [PLAY]. Hold [PTN] and press a trig key to cue that pattern: it takes over on the next step, at the step it would be on had it played since PLAY or the last normal pattern change.
Hold [PTN] and press [YES] again for DIRECT JUMP OFF: cued patterns wait for the end of the playing one again, as on the stock OS.

controls.name: DIRECT JUMP
controls.doc: Toggled with [PTN] + [YES]; a toast shows the new state. OFF at every power-on and not saved with the project. ON: a cued pattern takes over on the next step, clock-locked. OFF: stock pattern changes.

limitations: OS 1.40C. The author ran this version's native card image on his MKI (17 November 2026): the toggle, OFF at power-on, a Part-changing jump, other lengths and scales, a last-step cue, trig conditions with FILL and PRE, a jump after a normal pattern change, LFO AUTO CHANGE, SILENCE TRACKS, a Plays Free MIDI track and Direct Jump off all passed. On 19 November 2026 he ran the USB package ed3ba88a on the same MKI over a Modwerk development base (c889442d): installed and kept; a jump into another Part, the 16-12-12 restart case with its 1:2 hi-hat, a latched [FILL] and SILENCE TRACKS without a pop passed; after a power cycle it came back OFF and still installed; removed while ON and playing, [PTN] + [YES] was stock again; a trial left to roll back did. Not run on an MKII; the 0.1.x USB package ran on an MKII (toggle, jumps between a 64- and a 16-step pattern, a power cycle, removal).
OFF at every power-on and not stored in the project: turn it on again after a restart.
While the arranger or a pattern chain runs, pattern changes stay stock.

With differing track scales or lengths in PER TRACK mode, the jump waits for the next tick where every track is at a step boundary, at most one common step of all tracks' scales (24 clock ticks for 1x, 3/4x and 1/2x together).

With LFO AUTO CHANGE on, a track whose new pattern has trigs keeps the old Part's LFO setup until its first trig there; STOP, turning Direct Jump off or the next jump applies every waiting track at once.
[PTN] + [YES] no longer opens the pattern chooser on releasing [PTN]; [YES] alone and [PTN] with a trig key are unchanged.

Carries the author's fix for stock's MIDI Plays-Free stall (a Plays Free MIDI track with trig quantize DIRECT under PER TRACK scale stopped after its first step), whether Direct Jump is on or off. The bundle's other two fixes are not included.

A jump changes the Part through stock's own Part-change path, so stock's known Part-change carryover issues (a track going from PICKUP to FLEX can keep the old Part's pickup loop) happen on a jump as on a stock pattern change.
With Play Modes, each jump counts as a transport start for Play Modes, which restarts its own per-track state.

cpuPrice.conditions: MKI, development twin 87830783 of base c889442d (this branch's beta flags plus --dev), the author's project, bank A pattern A02 (12 steps) on Part 1 playing, 8 s per reading: frame interrupt 54.3 % before and installed (OFF, its power-on state), CPU meter 63.9 % both; with Direct Jump turned ON during a rolled-back trial 51.7 % and 62.0 %, against 51.7 % and 62.2/62.5 % without it right after. DSP cores within a point.

resources.recorded: 16 November 2026; source assembly, the native image of this module alone and the ColdFire port

storage.label: DRAM code and detours
storage.display: 4,000 B code and state + six 6 B detours + one 4 B pointer
storage.conditions: Two linked units in the DRAM reserve: Direct Jump's 3,938 bytes (code, two toast strings and 176 bytes of state) and the MIDI Plays-Free fix's 62 bytes of code; six six-byte detours over stock instructions and the [PTN]-layer YES press pointer. The USB package carries the units aligned, 4,546 bytes in all. No DSP memory, no saved data.

processing.label: ColdFire, per sequencer tick
processing.display: 30 instr. a tick OFF, 45 ON; at most 9,078 on a landing tick
processing.conditions: Authored instructions of the tick hook under ot_emu, worst at a cue that lands on its arming tick while all 16 tracks still wait for their first trig after the previous jump; the stock routines a landing calls (Program Change, the kernel posts, the per-track Part apply, the note-off) bring it to 17,225. While tracks wait for their first trig, up to 1,898 a tick. A stock pattern change adds 13 instructions (dj_swres) to stock's switch on that tick. The tick interrupt runs at level 3, below the DSP frame interrupt. Not chip timing.

impact.conditions: A jump to a pattern on another Part while playing, with LFO AUTO CHANGE and SILENCE TRACKS on: the landing tick and the tick after it, the dearest events. Between jumps, a short counter on every sequencer tick, and while tracks wait for their first trig in the new pattern a scan of the 16 tracks.

cpu.rationale: 30 executed instructions a sequencer tick while OFF and 45 while ON; up to 1,898 a tick while tracks wait for their first trig; at most 9,078 authored (17,225 with the stock routines it calls) on the tick a jump lands, and 13 on the tick of a stock pattern change (ot_emu). The tick interrupt runs at level 3, below the level-5 DSP frame interrupt. Under a 15 s MIDI flood with a jump every second, the longest frame interrupt was 1.0 us longer than the original OS's (156.7 us against 155.7 us in the port's time) and idle 0.30 points lower. Time on the unit is not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code and no change to the DSP programs.

memory.rationale: 4,000 bytes of ColdFire code and state in the DRAM reserve (176 bytes of state) and 40 bytes of stock writes; no DSP memory and no saved data.

cpuPrice.conditions: MKII, the owner's project Tresor Prep bank A pattern A01 Part 1 playing at 138 BPM (four-on-the-floor kick on T1, sample tracks sounding on T2, T5 and T6); FX1/FX2: T1 FILTER/NONE, T2 FILTER/DELAY, T3-T4 CHORUS/NONE, T5-T8 FILTER/DELAY; installed and not used by any key press, menu or setting; base development twin d3d71297 of base 0.7.8 (main 02dfa20ca); 8 s per reading. Frame interrupt 40.9 % before, 41 % installed and used nowhere; CPU meter 60.6 % before, 60.5 % at rest.

tests.summary: The author ran 0.2.0's native card image of this module alone on his MKI on 17 November 2026: all 13 checklist items passed (evidence/hardware.md). Under the ColdFire port (verify.py, 74 checks, all passed on that image): OFF identical to the original OS through a pattern change; four jumps (16 steps with [FILL] latched; 7 steps on Part 2; PER TRACK lengths and scales; a cue in the last step) whose sequencer state and trig-condition state equal a reference run of the incoming pattern since START on every tick after the landing; two jumps after a stock pattern change (12 steps at 1x after 12 at 1x; 3/4x after 2x) that equal a run which changed straight to the jump's pattern; each track's Part handed to the engine at its first sounding trig with LFO AUTO CHANGE on; the tracks SILENCE TRACKS silences released with stock's note-off the tick after the landing; and the MIDI Plays-Free stall, which the original OS shows and the module fixes. Before that he tested the same Direct Jump code in his own builds (15 and 16 November 2026); the 0.1.x USB package ran on the owner's MKII in October 2026. On 19 November 2026 he ran the USB package ed3ba88a on the same MKI over a Modwerk development base (c889442d): installed and kept; a jump into another Part, the 16-12-12 restart case with its 1:2 hi-hat, a latched [FILL] and SILENCE TRACKS without a pop passed; after a power cycle it came back OFF and still installed; removed while ON and playing, [PTN] + [YES] was stock again; a trial left to roll back did. CPU price on a development twin of that base (87830783), a 12-step pattern playing: 0.0 points of the frame interrupt, Direct Jump OFF and ON alike.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: jump between patterns on the next step
steps: Hold [PTN] and press [YES]: DIRECT JUMP ON appears. Release [PTN]; the pattern chooser stays shut.
Press [PLAY]. Hold [PTN] and press a trig key to cue that pattern: it takes over on the next step, at the step it would be on had it played since PLAY or the last normal pattern change.
Hold [PTN] and press [YES] again for DIRECT JUMP OFF: cued patterns wait for the end of the playing one again, as on the stock OS.

conditions.parameterExtremes: OFF, ON while idle, the tick that arms a jump, the landing tick and the tick after it, also after a stock pattern change (V7.3's restart frame); 16-step and 7-step (Part 2) patterns and a PER TRACK pattern with tracks from 2x to 1/8x; LFO AUTO CHANGE and SILENCE TRACKS on, all 16 tracks waiting for a trig, every MIDI LFO on a designer wave.
conditions.parameterModulation: Not applicable: one ON/OFF word toggled by a key gesture; no knob, lock, LFO or scene reaches it.
conditions.modeSwitching: Toggled ON and OFF while stopped and while playing; cues at the six phases of a step, re-jumps while every track still waits for its first trig, and jumps back to the previous pattern.
conditions.maxLoad: One instance per unit. Runs once per sequencer clock tick in the tick interrupt (level 3; its ICR read 3 in the port), below the level-5 DSP frame interrupt, which preempts it; its deadline is the next tick: 8.33 ms at the top tempo of 300 BPM (2,200,000 cycles at 264 MHz).
conditions.inputConditions: Authored instructions of dj_land per tick under ot_emu (PC watches on its entry and the hook's return, on each stock routine it calls and the unit's return site after it, and on the frame interrupt, whose instructions are removed when it preempts the tick), priced at 16 cycles each: at most 9,078 (145,248 cycles), on a cue that lands on its arming tick and first publishes 16 waiting tracks; 17,225 with the stock routines it calls, which are stock cost. Static bound from the source, every reachable routine and loop at its cap: 41,017 (656,272). dj_swres, outside dj_land in stock's switch block: 13, once per stock pattern change. Not chip timing.

regions.name: ColdFire code, two toast strings and 176 bytes of state (Direct Jump's linked unit, DRAM)
The MIDI Plays-Free fix's code (a second linked unit, DRAM)
Six six-byte detours and the four-byte [PTN]-layer YES pointer, written over stock in place

memory.conditions: From the two linked units (3,938 and 62 bytes of code and data, no bss; the USB package carries the same bytes aligned) and the seven stock writes. No DSP memory, no heap, no saved data.

hardware.summary: The author flashed the native card image of this module alone (OCTATRACK_MW_DJK73B.bin, MAIN OS a7074bfd, OS VERSION MW_DJK73B; DIRECT JUMP V7.3 byte for byte) on his MKI and reported all 13 checklist items passed: boot; the [PTN] + [YES] toggle and toast with the chooser shut; OFF after a power cycle; a jump into a pattern on another Part; jumps between other lengths and into PER TRACK scales, landing where the pattern would be since PLAY or the last normal pattern change; a cue in the last step on its grid point; 1:2 and 1:4 trigs in step across jumps, a latched [FILL] kept and a PRE trig played; a jump after a normal change from a 16-step A01 to a 12-step A02 landing a 12-step A03 in phase with A02, its 1:2 hi-hat in step; LFO AUTO CHANGE with a ringing sample; no pop with SILENCE TRACKS; a Plays Free MIDI track in PER TRACK mode; Direct Jump off as stock; nothing odd.
limitations: The card image above; the shipped USB package ed3ba88a, built from the same source, ran on the same MKI over a Modwerk development base c889442d on 19 November 2026 (evidence/hardware.md, TESTING.md): installed and kept, a jump into another Part, the 16-12-12 restart case, a latched [FILL], SILENCE TRACKS without a pop, OFF and still installed after a power cycle, removal while ON and playing, a rolled-back trial.
MKI only; not run on an MKII.
A functional report: the project, how long it ran and whether external MIDI gear was attached are not stated; nothing timed or recorded.
